groups.title: Cold Relief Capsule
groups.efficacy: This medicine is used to relieve the various symptoms of a cold (runny nose, nasal congestion, sneezing, sore throat, cough, phlegm, chills, fever, headache, joint pain and muscle pain).
groups.usage: For people aged 15 years and over and adults, 2 capsules per dose; for people aged 8 years to under 15 years, 1 capsule per dose, 3 times a day, 30 minutes after meals.
groups.caution: Anyone who regularly drinks 3 or more glasses of alcohol a day should consult a doctor or pharmacist before taking this medicine or any other antipyretic analgesic, as it may cause liver damage. Very rarely, serious and potentially fatal skin reactions have been reported; stop taking it immediately if a rash or other sign of hypersensitivity appears.

summaryTable.Use: Cold symptoms: runny nose, congestion, sore throat, cough, fever, aches
summaryTable.Check with a pharmacist: Under 8 years; regular alcohol use; serious skin reactions

groups.title: Mucolytic Capsule
groups.efficacy: This medicine is used as a mucolytic and expectorant in acute and chronic respiratory disease.
groups.usage: For adults, 300 mg 2 to 3 times a day by mouth. For acute respiratory disease, do not take it continuously for 10 days or more.
groups.caution: Do not take if you are hypersensitive to this medicine, or have liver cirrhosis, cystathionine synthase deficiency, peptic ulcer, severe renal impairment or severe hepatic impairment, or if you are pregnant or may be pregnant. Before taking it, consult a doctor or pharmacist.

summaryTable.Use: Mucolytic and expectorant in acute and chronic respiratory disease
summaryTable.Check with a pharmacist: Liver cirrhosis, peptic ulcer, severe renal or hepatic impairment, pregnancy

groups.title: Antidiarrhoeal Capsule
groups.efficacy: This medicine is used for diarrhoea, diarrhoea with abdominal pain, a feeling of heaviness, loose stools and vomiting with diarrhoea.
groups.usage: For people aged 15 years and over, 2 capsules 3 times a day. Leave an interval of at least 4 hours between doses.
groups.caution: Do not take if you are pregnant or may be pregnant, are breastfeeding, are a newborn or a child aged 7 years or under, or have galactose intolerance, Lapp lactase deficiency or a related genetic problem. Before taking it, consult a doctor or pharmacist.

summaryTable.Use: Diarrhoea, loose stools, abdominal pain with diarrhoea
summaryTable.Check with a pharmacist: Age 7 years or under; pregnancy, breastfeeding; galactose intolerance

groups.title: Combined Oral Contraceptive Tablet
groups.efficacy: This medicine is used for contraception.
groups.usage: Take 1 tablet a day for 21 days in the order shown, then have a 7-day break. It is best to take it at about the same time each day. Menstruation occurs during the 7-day break and usually starts 2 to 3 days after the last tablet. Refer to the detailed approved product information.
groups.caution: Because the risk of serious cardiovascular events such as thrombosis may increase, women taking an oral contraceptive should refrain from smoking. Smokers aged 35 years and over must not take this medicine. Before taking it, consult a doctor or pharmacist.

summaryTable.Use: Contraception
summaryTable.Check with a pharmacist: Smoking at 35 years and over; thrombosis risk

groups.title: Cough and Phlegm Capsule
groups.efficacy: This medicine is used for cough and phlegm.
groups.usage: For people aged 15 years and over and adults, 2 capsules per dose; for people aged 8 years to under 15 years, 1 capsule per dose, 3 times a day.
groups.caution: Do not take if you are hypersensitive to this medicine or have experienced such hypersensitivity, are pregnant or may be pregnant, are a child under 2 years or an infant under 3 months, or have galactose intolerance and related genetic problems. Before taking it, consult a doctor or pharmacist.

summaryTable.Use: Cough and phlegm
summaryTable.Check with a pharmacist: Under 2 years; pregnancy; galactose intolerance

groups.title: Low-dose Aspirin Enteric-coated Tablet
groups.efficacy: This medicine is used to inhibit thrombus formation in myocardial infarction, cerebral infarction and unstable angina, to inhibit thrombus formation after coronary artery bypass grafting (CABG) or percutaneous transluminal coronary angioplasty (PTCA), and to reduce cardiovascular risk in high-risk patients.
groups.usage: For adults, 1 tablet once a day. As this is an enteric-coated tablet, it may be taken before a meal with plenty of water.
groups.caution: Do not take if you are hypersensitive to this medicine or to other salicylates, or if you have peptic ulcer, aspirin-induced asthma or a history of it, haemophilia, severe hepatic impairment, severe renal impairment or severe cardiac insufficiency. Before taking it, consult a doctor or pharmacist.

summaryTable.Use: Prevention of thrombus formation; cardiovascular risk reduction
summaryTable.Check with a pharmacist: Peptic ulcer; aspirin asthma; severe hepatic or renal impairment

groups.title: Digestive and Laxative Tablet
groups.efficacy: This medicine is used for loss of appetite, abdominal bloating, abnormal intestinal fermentation and haemorrhoids.
groups.usage: For adults (aged 15 years and over), 1 to 2 tablets 2 times a day, before meals, with meals, between meals or after meals. Leave an interval of at least 4 hours between doses. Start with the smallest amount and increase or decrease it gradually while watching the shape and condition of the stool.
groups.caution: Do not take if you have an acute abdominal condition (appendicitis, intestinal bleeding, ulcerative colitis and similar), intestinal obstruction, or if you are a child aged 7 years or under. Before taking it, consult a doctor or pharmacist.

summaryTable.Use: Loss of appetite, abdominal bloating, abnormal fermentation, haemorrhoids
summaryTable.Check with a pharmacist: Age 7 years or under; acute abdominal disease; bowel obstruction

groups.title: Children's Ibuprofen Syrup
groups.efficacy: This medicine is used to reduce fever caused by acute upper respiratory tract infection.
groups.usage: For children aged 6 months and over, 0.4 to 0.6 mL/kg (5 to 7 mg/kg) per dose, every 4 to 6 hours as needed, not exceeding 4 doses a day (28 mg/kg). For children weighing 30 kg or less, do not exceed a maximum of 25 mL (300 mg) a day.
groups.caution: Anyone who regularly drinks 3 or more glasses of alcohol a day should consult a doctor or pharmacist before taking this medicine or any other antipyretic analgesic, as it may cause gastrointestinal bleeding. Before taking it, consult a doctor or pharmacist.

summaryTable.Use: Fever from acute upper respiratory tract infection in children
summaryTable.Check with a pharmacist: Under 6 months; maximum 4 doses a day; gastrointestinal bleeding

groups.title: Analgesic Tablet for Neuralgia
groups.efficacy: This medicine is used for neuralgia, low back pain and stiff shoulders.
groups.usage: For adults, 1 to 2 tablets 2 times a day, when pain or an attack occurs.
groups.caution: Before taking it, consult a doctor or pharmacist if the person is an infant, young child or child aged 14 years or under who has or is suspected of having chickenpox or influenza, or if you have an allergic constitution. If there is no improvement after taking it several times, stop taking it and consult a doctor or pharmacist.

summaryTable.Use: Neuralgia, low back pain, stiff shoulders
summaryTable.Check with a pharmacist: Age 14 years or under with chickenpox or influenza; allergic constitution

groups.title: Acid Reducer Tablet
groups.efficacy: This medicine is used to relieve heartburn associated with excess stomach acid.
groups.usage: For adults and people aged 15 years and over, 1 tablet per dose. Do not take more than 2 tablets within 24 hours.
groups.caution: Do not take if you are hypersensitive to this medicine, or have galactose intolerance, Lapp lactase deficiency, or a genetic problem such as glucose-galactose malabsorption. Before taking it, consult a doctor or pharmacist.

summaryTable.Use: Heartburn associated with excess stomach acid

groups.usage: For adults, 0.5 to 1 tablet (50 to 100 mg) 1 to 3 times a day. It may be adjusted appropriately according to age and symptoms.
groups.caution: Do not take if you have galactose intolerance, Lapp lactase deficiency, or a genetic problem such as glucose-galactose malabsorption.

groups.title: Antihistamine Tablet
groups.efficacy: This medicine is used for seasonal and perennial allergic rhinitis, allergic conjunctivitis, chronic idiopathic urticaria and skin itching, and for eczema and dermatitis (when used together with a topical hydrocortisone preparation).
groups.usage: For adults and children aged 6 years and over, 1 tablet (10 mg) once a day at bedtime. Patients sensitive to adverse reactions take 0.5 tablet (5 mg) split into a morning and an evening dose. It may be adjusted appropriately according to age and symptoms.
groups.caution: Do not take if you are hypersensitive to this medicine or to hydroxyzine or piperazine derivatives or have experienced such hypersensitivity, or have renal failure (creatinine clearance < 10 mL/min). Before taking it, consult a doctor or pharmacist.

summaryTable.Use: Allergic rhinitis, allergic conjunctivitis, chronic urticaria, skin itching
summaryTable.Check with a pharmacist: Under 6 years; renal failure

groups.usage: Take 2 to 4 capsules (1000 to 2000 mg) a day, on 10 to 20 days of each month.
groups.caution: Do not take if you have severe renal impairment or hepatic coma, are a child aged 6 years or under, have cystinuria, or are hypersensitive to soybean oil, soya or peanut. Before taking it, consult a doctor or pharmacist.
